source_text: Bohra representatives and supporters consistently reject equivalence to severe forms of female genital mutilation, such as African infibulation (WHO Type III), portraying khatna instead as a benign, non-deforming ritual confined to the prepuce without removal of the clitoris or labia, and arguing that anti-FGM campaigns conflate it with more harmful variants to impose external moral judgments.
